questions.question: Which of the following Mauryan inscriptions is NOT located in present-day India?

__

• Kandahar is currently in modern-day Afghanistan.
 
• The other inscriptions mentioned (Kalsi, Maski, and Girnar) are all located within the geographical boundaries of present-day India.
 
• The Mauryan Empire, under rulers such as Ashoka, had inscriptions spread across a vast region, including parts of present-day India, Nepal, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Mauryan Empire** was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE and became one of the largest empires in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Ashoka, one of the most famous Mauryan emperors, is known for his widespread inscriptions and promotion of Buddhism.
 
• The inscriptions of Ashoka, written in various scripts and languages, are key historical sources for understanding the Mauryan period.
 
• These inscriptions were often engraved on rocks and pillars and served to propagate the policies and edicts of Ashoka, including his advocacy for dharma (moral law) and non-violence.

• The act extends to the whole of India and applies to all banking companies.
 
• It has been amended several times to address the changing needs and challenges of the banking sector.
 
• One significant amendment was made in 1965, which brought cooperative banks under the purview of the act.
 
• The act also lays down the procedure for the amalgamation and winding up of banks.
 
• The RBI has the authority to issue directives, inspect banks, and take necessary actions to ensure the stability and efficiency of the banking system.

questions.question: Which of the parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. They are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• The Directive Principles include provisions for securing and protecting a social order, right to work, education, and public assistance in certain cases, provision for just and humane conditions of work, and more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• **The Directive Principles are inspired by the Directive Principles of Social Policy** enumerated in the Irish Constitution.
 
• **They aim to establish a welfare state by securing a social order based on social, economic, and political justice.**

questions.question: In any tennis game, if both players win three points each in a game (i.e. score is 40-40), then it's called a __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deuce**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In tennis, a score of 40-40 is referred to as a **deuce**.
 
• When the score reaches deuce, a player must win two consecutive points to win the game.
 
• The first point won after deuce is called "advantage." If the player with the advantage wins the next point, they win the game; if they lose it, the score returns to deuce.
 
• This rule ensures that a player must lead by two points to secure a game after reaching deuce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"deuce"** is derived from the Old French word "deus" meaning two, indicating that two more points are needed to win the game from this score.
 
• Tennis scoring can trace its origins back to medieval France, and the unique terms and scoring system have been retained over centuries.
 
• Understanding the concept of deuce is fundamental for anyone learning the rules and structure of tennis matches.

questions.question: In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then known elements in the order of __________. It is known as 'Newlands' Law of Octaves'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increasing atomic masses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then known elements in the order of **increasing atomic masses**.
 
• This arrangement is known as **Newlands' Law of Octaves**.
 
• According to this law, every eighth element had properties similar to that of the first, much like the octaves in music.
 
• Newlands' Law of Octaves was one of the earliest attempts to classify elements based on their properties and atomic masses.
 
• This law was applicable only up to calcium, as beyond calcium, the properties of elements did not match the pattern.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• John Newlands' classification was an important step towards the development of the modern periodic table.
 
• Later, Dmitri Mendeleev and others improved upon Newlands' ideas, leading to the periodic table we use today.
 
• The periodic table is now based on the **increasing atomic number**, not atomic mass.
 
• Newlands' work demonstrated the periodicity of elements' properties, which is a fundamental concept in chemistry.
